newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU to start on time with many countries - De Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EMU to start on time with many countries - De Silguy.

text.p: European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday he expected economic and monetary union to start on schedule with many countries.
"It is clear that EMU will become reality starting January 1, 1999 and that a significant number of countries will join then," he told a news conference while on a visit to Finland.
"There is no turning back," he said. "That point has been crossed."
He said he could not predict "from any crystal ball" which or how many countries would form the currency union at the start.
But European growth had been strong, and many countries had shown "substantial budget discipline".
This included Italy, Spain and Portugal, he said in response to a question.
He declined to comment on any individual country's chance of qualifying for monetary union, but said Finland was in a "very good position" to be in the first wave.
He also declined any comment on remarks made by Bank of France Council Member Paul Marchelli earlier on Friday about a desirable level for the euro.
